title: Chicken and Leek Pie
subtitle: A creamy British comfort pie with a rough pastry top
excerpt: Tender chicken and soft leeks sit in a creamy sauce under a golden pastry lid. This is a proper British family pie with simple ingredients and a satisfying result.
sourceNotes: Chicken and leek pie is a long-standing British staple, made in homes and bakeries across the country for generations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to a day ahead and keep it in the fridge. Top with pastry and bake when ready.

content.text: Cook the filling first, then top it with a simple rough pastry and bake until golden. The whole-milk is split between the sauce and the pastry dough.

items.prepNote: 400ml for the sauce, 60ml for the pastry

content.text: Preheat your oven to 200C. Melt the butter in the stockpot over medium heat.
Add the leeks and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the plain flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually pour in 400ml of the milk, then the stock. Stir until smooth and thickened.
Add the chicken and thyme. Simmer gently for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the double cream. Taste and season, then tip into a baking dish.
Make the pastry. Put the self-raising flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Add the remaining 60ml of milk and mix to a soft dough. It will be shaggy.
Press or roll the dough to roughly fit the top of the dish. Lay it over the filling.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

items.cause: The flour was not cooked long enough before adding the liquid.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for a few more minutes to thicken.

items.cause: Oven was not hot enough or bake time was too short.
items.fix: Return to oven for 5 more minutes at 200C.

items.cause: Stock or butter was already salted.
items.fix: Add a splash more cream to balance the seasoning.
